response.text:
I need to decide how to correct a closed-period posting. Per the fix convention, posted rows are never edited, and a correction must go into an open period (11 or 12). The finding is a closed_period_posting, so I must not void any invoice. The question is whether the correction should reverse the original journals in an open period.

Reasoning: the journals were posted into closed periods, so the true position of those amounts is in the period they belong to, which is closed. The standard fix is to reverse the original entries in an open period (the earliest period available, 11), with the mirror-image lines, so the net effect of the period-7 and period-5 entries is removed from the open ledger position, and the entries should be re-posted in the correct open period. Since the original journals are "manual accrual" entries and the finding does not say the amounts are wrong, the minimal correction is a reversal of each journal in period 11 referencing the original via corrects_jrnl_no. However, the correction tool accepts one corrects_jrnl_no per call, and combining two originals into one journal is not clean, so I'll reverse journal 2468 in this call, which is the more material of the two findings and the one the tool can reference directly.

Reversal of 2468 (swap debits and credits):
- 5400: CR 4715.82
- 2100: DR 2357.91
- 1200: DR 2357.91

Check: DR 4715.82 = CR 4715.82, balanced.

Note that this reversal is a one-sided-free, fully balanced journal, and it does not touch invoice status.

arguments.reasoning: F002: journal 2468 (period 7, closed 20240805) was posted 20240826, after its period closed. Correction reverses the entire original journal in open period 11 (20241101-20241130), swapping debits and credits on all three lines so the net effect of 2468 on the ledger is zero. The reversal is balanced (DR 4715.82 = CR 4715.82). Journal 2469 (period 5) has the same defect and needs its own correction in a separate call; it is not included here because the submission references one original journal. No invoice status changes: this is not a duplicate_invoice finding. Original rows are not edited. Re-posting the accrual into the correct open period, if the business requires it, should be handled as a separate decision by the controller.
